title: Melanocyte conversion is all-or-none per animal, stochastic only across the cohort

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Melanocyte conversion is all-or-none per animal, stochastic only across the cohort

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Melanocyte conversion after instructor-cell depolarization is a collective, all-or-none decision: different reagents give different incidences in a cohort (e.g. 70% converted), but each animal is either fully converted or fully normal; a computational model fitted to these incidences predicted interventions (two drugs and a dominant-negative construct) that were then confirmed to produce the first partially converted animals.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › From normal melanocytes to a melanoma phenotype: a collective decision

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Using different reagents could induce different incidences of hyperpigmentation (conversion) in a cohort of animals, but this was a population-level phenotype: for example, 70% of the animals could be converted, but any given animal was either fully converted or fully normal (Fig. 4a, b).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: McMillen P, Levin M, “Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates”, Communications biology (2024), doi:10.1038/s42003-024-06037-4; section “Introduction › From normal melanocytes to a melanoma phenotype: a collective decision”. Scope: Xenopus laevis tadpoles with perturbed instructor-cell bioelectric signalling

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-collective-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: All-or-none conversion and emergence of partial animals have direct criteria, while held-out interventions provide genuine discrimination. Public summaries permit checking the pattern but may not support a complete independent model audit.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Score within-animal melanocyte conversion continuously across perturbations, fit the published signaling model to cohort incidence, and test its preregistered partial-conversion predictions against intervention outcomes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Animal-level raw scores and executable model code may not be public.

Retrospective model fitting can overstate prediction.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: All-or-none scoring per animal, cohort incidence and a predicted partial-conversion intervention are all decidable if the per-animal table and the model are public. The review states the pattern and the successful prediction; the underlying scores and code are not an open deposit. A reanalysis can use the published incidences only as summaries, so both the concordance claim and the model confirmation stay partly out of reach. This was one of the harder items because model completeness cannot be judged from the review text alone.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Score each tadpole as fully converted, fully normal or partial, under each reagent, and compare the within-animal pattern with a binomial model of independent melanocytes. All-or-none animals at varying cohort rates would support collective concordance. Re-implementing the published signaling model should then predict the drug and dominant-negative conditions under which partial animals appear; failure of those conditions, or partial animals in the original reagents, would refute the joint claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
It is unclear from the review alone whether the model equations are complete enough to re-run without the original code.

Fully versus partially converted depends on a threshold applied to images.

Per-animal conversion scores and the model parameter file are not in a public repository.
